subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC / on-prem requirements
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Danielle Ross <dross@finhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC / on-prem requirements

Hi Danielle —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our discovery so everyone is aligned and we can prioritize next steps. Please correct me if I missed anything.

Summary of pain and goals
- Regulated workload (PHI) requires customer-managed network boundaries and strict audit/retention controls.
- Current inference environment is on-prem with limited burst capacity; looking for predictable SLA-backed inference for peak billing cycles.
- Primary goals: data isolation, key management (BYOK/KMS/HSM), and clear audit trails for token-level access.

Current stack + constraints
- Inference today: on-prem GPU cluster (NVIDIA A100), internal model serving (v1.2).
- Network: no public internet access on inference hosts; only a controlled egress through a bastion/proxy.
- Identity: Okta SSO for engineers; customer wants service accounts scoped to audit logs.

Success criteria for Phase 1 (POC)
- Deployment of Redwood Private into FinHealth VPC or air-gapped on-prem with customer-managed keys.
- End-to-end demo generating sample PHI-safe inference with preserved audit logs and retention policy.
- Latency < 150ms p95 for typical inference payloads; throughput target ~200 reqs/min initially.

Risks / open questions
- Air-gap: do you require a fully disconnected deployment (no occassional pull updates) or is a controlled pull from an approved staging network acceptable?
- KMS: preferred vendor (AWS KMS vs. Azure Key Vault vs. on-prem HSM)?
- Network egress: will the bastion/proxy allow outbound to Redwood control-plane endpoints, or will we need a private control plane deployment?

Next steps
1) FinHealth to share the security questionnaire + network diagram (we flagged these on the call). (Danielle)
2) Redwood to schedule a technical deep-dive with Aditya and Dev to validate network and KMS options (Marissa to coordinate).
3) Align on POC success metrics and timeline; target kickoff the week of 7/27.

Attachments: FinHealth_Network_Requirements.pdf (network diagram template)

If that looks right, I can send calendar invites for the deep-dive and the POC kickoff.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0132
From: Danielle Ross <dross@finhealth.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinHealth Procurement <procurement@finhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 17:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC / on-prem requirements

Marissa —

Thanks for the clear summary. This matches my notes. A few clarifications and answers to your open questions:

- Air-gap: we need a deployment that can operate in a mostly air-gapped mode. Occasional signed "pulls" from an approved update bucket are acceptable, but there must be an option for a completely offline install for the most sensitive clusters.
- KMS: primary preference is AWS KMS, but we have an on-prem Thales HSM for the regulated cluster which we may need to use.
- Network egress: the inference hosts cannot reach the public internet directly. We can provide a managed proxy/bastion that allows authenticated outbound to specific endpoints.

I've attached the initial security questionnaire and our internal network diagram for the cluster. Procurement is looped here; they will want vendor and licensing details for Redwood Private and any managed service options.

Attachments: FinHealth_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx, FinHealth_Cluster_Diagram.pdf

I'll review proposed dates for the week of 7/27 and come back with availability.

Thanks,
Danielle Ross
Head of Infrastructure, FinHealth
dross@finhealth.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 21 Jul 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC / on-prem requirements

Aditya / Dev —

Forwarding FinHealth's reply and attachments. High level asks: air-gap-capable deployment, AWS KMS support plus on-prem HSM integration, and no direct internet from inference hosts (we'll need a proxy or private control plane).

Proposed technical deep-dive goals (45-60m):
- Confirm whether Redwood Private can be installed fully offline and what components require outbound connectivity.
- Walk through KMS integration flow (AWS KMS, HSM options) and key rotation model.
- Validate audit log collection and retention options (token-level visibility).
- Network design: proxy/bastion patterns vs private control plane.

Can we target Wed 7/29 10:00am PT for the session? Dev, can you lead the HSM/KMS discussion; Aditya can cover control-plane and private deployment model.

Also adding a checklist for items we'll need from FinHealth before POC: completed security questionnaire, network ACLs and proxy egress rules, list of service accounts and Okta scoping, preferred KMS vendor details.

Thanks  I want to make sure we come prepared to validate the air-gap story.

Marissa
From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2026 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Discovery recap: FinHealth Private VPC / on-prem requirements

Sounds good — I can run the HSM/KMS part and sketch the integration options:
- AWS KMS: standard envelope encryption; we support grants for service accounts and can rotate CMKs with minimal downtime.
- On-prem HSM (Thales): we'll need an HSM connector running in the customer network and a small agent to proxy signing requests; will confirm security model for offline installs.
- Air-gap: we have an "airgap bundle" that includes all runtime artifacts and a signed update mechanism; full offline install is possible but will require an on-site engineer for initial setup.

I’ll prepare a short diagram and a checklist of ports/endpoints the installer will need. Wed 7/29 10:00am PT works for me.

- Dev
